answers: The "angst" travelers feel at overcrowded gates may soon be eased at United Airlines terminals, an exec for the airline says. That's because United just began a new initiative designed to relieve that particular "passenger pain point," as CNBC puts it, by changing up its departure protocol: The number of boarding lines has been cut from five to two, and overeager customers are now asked to stay out of the boarding area until their boarding group (one of six in total, including pre-boarders) is announced. "It's too congested," a UA rep says of the current procedure, which often results in arriving fliers having to push their way through throngs of departing ones. Forbes notes customers can also opt in to receive push notifications via the mobile app, meaning they can hang out in nearby restaurants or shops until they receive an alert on their cellphones that it's time to board. Over the past year, United test-drove a variety of boarding options on about 12,000 flights, ending up with this system, which is similar to the way American, Delta, and Southwest queue up. United has been using the procedure at LAX since winter and will now implement it at all locations, per USA Today. It's also spreading passengers around more equitably within its six boarding groups, which includes pre-boarders (e.g., families with young kids, service members), first-class passengers and frequent fliers in groups 1 and 2, and then everyone else in groups 3, 4, and 5. "The boarding process was one of the top areas customers told us they wanted improved," another UA rep says in a statement, noting customer and employee feedback guided the airline on the enhancements. (United had some "unfortunate dog incidents" earlier this year.)

full.prediction:
**Summary of News Passages**

United Airlines has recently implemented a new boarding process aimed at reducing congestion and improving the overall boarding experience for passengers. The airline has transitioned from using five boarding lanes to just two, with the goal of streamlining the process and minimizing delays. This change, which is now in effect at all United gates, involves a color-coded system with two lanes—blue and green—where passengers are divided into five boarding groups. Groups 1 and 2, which include elite members, frequent flyers, and priority passengers, will board through the blue lane, while Groups 3, 4, and 5 will use the green lane. Passengers not actively boarding are encouraged to remain seated until their group is called.

In addition to the new boarding process, United has introduced push notifications for passengers using the airline’s mobile app. These alerts will notify travelers when boarding begins, helping to reduce the need for them to gather around the gate and potentially easing congestion. The airline also mentioned that Chase co-branded credit card holders will be included in Group 2, offering them priority access.

This update follows months of testing in select gates in Chicago and Houston, and it is part of a broader trend among airlines to improve the boarding process. American Airlines and Delta Air Lines have already adopted similar strategies, with American using a two-lane system and Delta using four lanes. United’s new process also allows top-tier elite members, known as "1K" members, to pre-board before the official process starts, a feature not commonly offered by other carriers.

The changes come in response to customer feedback and the challenges of managing large numbers of passengers efficiently. United has noted that overcrowding at gates has been a growing concern, with passengers often spilling into corridors and creating delays. The airline has also acknowledged that many travelers still feel the need to stand in line to secure their spot, even with the new system in place.

In addition to the boarding process changes, United has announced a significant partnership with Copa Airlines and Avianca Airlines. The three carriers have reached an agreement to form a joint business alliance (JBA) that will integrate their route networks and offer customers more seamless service, new nonstop routes, and competitive fares. The JBA is expected to provide substantial benefits to customers, communities, and the marketplace, including increased competition and improved travel experiences. However, the agreement is pending regulatory approval and antitrust immunity from the U.S. Department of Transportation.

Overall, these updates reflect United’s ongoing efforts to enhance the customer experience,
